recommendations.name: ‘AMA‘AMA – Contemporary Island Cooking
recommendations.reason: Mina's Fish House (5/5, 4km away) is the clearest single signal in their file - oceanfront terrace, careful plating, fish-forward, fine for a celebration - and ‘AMA‘AMA at Aulani is the same format on the same stretch of Ko Olina coast: open-air lanai tables facing the lagoon, a kitchen built around local fish, and the resort-validated parking they specifically praised at Mina's. It also fixes what dragged Roy's Ko Olina down to vibe 2 for them.
recommendations.avoids: Unlike Monkeypod Kitchen in Kapolei (their 3/5, 'music was too loud') and Restaurant 604 (quiet 1), this is a table-service dining room with ambient surf rather than amplified music - their top dealbreaker is noise, and this is the calmest fine-dining room in Ko Olina.
recommendations.dish: Whole or filleted local catch with island accompaniments; the poke and limu starter is the honest opener
recommendations.diet_fit: Menu is fish-led: fresh catch of the day, ahi poke, seafood appetizers, and vegetable-forward island sides, so the pescatarian in the party has several substantial mains without touching the meat section.

recommendations.name: Kahumana - Organic Farm & Café
recommendations.reason: Every high score they gave rests on food 5 plus a calm, pretty setting - Mina's Fish House and Rigo Spanish Italian both got vibe 5. Kahumana is the West Side answer: a working organic farm in Lualualei with open-air seating looking at the Waianae range, produce walked in from the field, and the kind of unhurried service that earned Olay's and Onkee their service 5s. It is also the one pick that guarantees the pescatarian a full menu rather than a workaround.
recommendations.avoids: Steers wide of the loud-music problem that capped Monkeypod Kitchen at 3/5 - there is no bar scene here at all, it is a daytime farm café where the ambient noise is birds.
recommendations.dish: The farm plate with whatever greens and root vegetables came out of the field that week
recommendations.diet_fit: Largely vegetarian/vegan kitchen with fish specials - farm salads, curries, veggie burgers and grain bowls are all full mains for a pescatarian.

recommendations.name: Taste of Hong Kong
recommendations.reason: They rate cooking above decor (Katsumidori got food 5 with vibe 2 and still 4/5), and they clearly like a kitchen that does one tradition properly - Olay's Thai Lao, Onkee Korean. Cantonese seafood cookery is the gap in their library: steamed whole fish and clay-pot tofu are the closest thing to Mina's respect for fish in a neighbourhood-price setting, and it is 6km from home rather than a drive into town.
recommendations.avoids: Not a bar-grill with a sound system like Monkeypod Kapolei; a plain dining room where conversation carries. I do not have first-hand knowledge of this specific venue's food, so I am flagging that rather than overselling it.
recommendations.diet_fit: Cantonese menus of this type reliably carry steamed fish with ginger and scallion, salt-and-pepper shrimp, braised tofu with mushrooms and stir-fried greens with garlic - all substantial pescatarian mains. Worth confirming the fish list by phone.

recommendations.name: Thai Pho
recommendations.reason: Olay's Thai Lao is a 5/5 they return to for tom yum and curries - that is a taste for chili heat, lemongrass and herbs, not for Thai restaurants as a category. This is the nearest kitchen working in that register (7km, versus 23km to Olay's), and the Vietnamese half of the menu adds the herb-plate and tamarind-sour side of the same flavour family.
recommendations.avoids: A small counter-service dining room rather than the loud, music-driven rooms that sank Monkeypod Kitchen and Restaurant 604 for them.
recommendations.diet_fit: Tom yum and tom kha can be ordered with shrimp, green and red curry with tofu or fish, papaya salad, and pho can be had in the seafood or vegetable-broth versions - ask for the veg broth to be safe. I don't know this specific kitchen, so confirm broth on arrival.

recommendations.name: Paesano
recommendations.reason: Three of their Italian meals scored well - cino (4, 'authentic'), Giovedi (4), Rigo (5) - but cino lost points for a dark interior and Giovedi for parking. Paesano in Mililani is the mid-island version: an old-line family Italian room with easy free parking, half the drive of the Honolulu Italians, and the seafood pastas that connect to their Mina's/Rigo thread.
recommendations.avoids: Avoids the no-free-parking annoyance they noted at Giovedi and Olay's, and it is a quiet suburban dining room rather than a noisy bar-restaurant like Restaurant 604.
recommendations.diet_fit: Italian-American seafood section: linguine with clams, shrimp scampi, cioppino-style seafood pasta, plus eggplant parmigiana and marinara/pesto pastas - multiple real mains for the pescatarian.

recommendations.name: Sushi Sho
recommendations.reason: Kaiten Sushi Ginza Onodera is their only food-5-plus-service-5-plus-vibe-4 sushi score, and Katsumidori proved they will forgive a tired room for good fish. Sushi Sho is the logical step up rather than a fifth conveyor-belt stop: an edomae omakase counter with aged and cured nigiri, a chef talking you through each piece - which is exactly the 'super friendly, always fresh' experience they praised at Onodera, done at the highest level on the island.
recommendations.avoids: Completely sidesteps the noise problem that gave Restaurant 604 quiet 1 - it is a hushed counter of a dozen-odd seats - and it also fixes the 'interior outdated' complaint they had about Katsumidori and Roy's.
recommendations.dish: The omakase as served; the saba and the marinated tuna nigiri are the signatures
recommendations.diet_fit: An all-fish omakase - nigiri, sashimi, chawanmushi, tamago and vegetable side dishes. Nothing in the progression is meat or poultry, so this is one of the safest pescatarian rooms in Honolulu.

recommendations.name: Sasabune
recommendations.reason: Their sushi ratings reward freshness and a chef's guidance (Onodera 5/5, 'always fresh, super friendly'). Sasabune is a 'trust me' house where the chef sends courses in sequence with warm rice - a different discipline from the kaiten belt at Onodera and the tablet ordering at Katsumidori, so it extends the thread instead of repeating it.
recommendations.avoids: Small, calm counter-and-tables room - the opposite of the too-noisy Restaurant 604, their lowest-rated meal.
recommendations.dish: The omakase progression; the halibut with ponzu and the blue crab hand roll are the standouts
recommendations.diet_fit: Fish-only menu: nigiri and sashimi courses, hand rolls, miso soup and vegetable small plates. No meat dishes to navigate.

recommendations.name: Yohei Sushi
recommendations.reason: A neighbourhood Kapalama counter with a serious traditional chef - it lands squarely between Onodera (5/5, friendliness and freshness) and Katsumidori (food 5) while beating both on the thing they never scored well: a calm room with a chef who remembers you. Local-catch nigiri here speaks to the same island-fish appreciation that made Mina's Fish House a 5.
recommendations.avoids: Avoids the outdated-and-charmless room they knocked Katsumidori Sushi Tokyo and Roy's Ko Olina for; it's a quiet, tidy sushi-ya with proper counter seating, and free-ish street parking unlike Giovedi.
recommendations.dish: Nigiri set with local kumu or onaga, and the negitoro
recommendations.diet_fit: Nigiri, sashimi, chirashi bowls, sunomono and agedashi tofu - a complete pescatarian meal with no adaptation needed.

recommendations.name: MW Restaurant
recommendations.reason: Roy's Ko Olina got food 5 from them but only vibe 2 and value 3 - they liked the modern Hawaii-regional cooking and the dessert work and wished the room matched. MW is precisely that dish repaired: the same refined local-fish-and-local-produce cooking, famous pastry program, but in a bright contemporary dining room. Pair it with their Mina's Fish House 5 and this is the safest high-end pick in town for them.
recommendations.avoids: Fixes the dated interior that capped Roy's Ko Olina at vibe 2, and it is a conversational dining room, not a music-driven one like Monkeypod Kitchen.
recommendations.dish: Mochi-crusted local fish, and the candy bar dessert
recommendations.diet_fit: Always has a market fish main plus seafood starters (poke, ahi) and vegetable-forward dishes; the kitchen is used to building a pescatarian plate. Ask which catch is on that night.

recommendations.name: Mud Hen Water
recommendations.reason: This is the thinking eater's version of what they enjoyed at The Kini Room (vibe 5, value 5, great mocktails) crossed with the island cooking of Mina's Fish House: small plates built on kalo, limu, poi and local fish, an inventive non-alcoholic drink list, and a low-key Kaimuki room with an open patio. Mocktails show up in three of their five-star notes, and this kitchen takes them seriously.
recommendations.avoids: Unlike Monkeypod Kitchen and Restaurant 604, there is no live band or sports-bar volume here - it's a small neighbourhood dining room where the table talk is the loudest thing.
recommendations.dish: Limu and poi with fresh catch; the kalo dishes are the reason to come
recommendations.diet_fit: Menu rotates but reliably carries fresh local fish, poke-style raw preparations, and several taro/vegetable small plates that add up to a full pescatarian meal. Confirm the night's fish selection.

recommendations.name: Mimi's Peruvian Cuisine
recommendations.reason: The single strongest pattern in their file is raw and cooked fish done with acidity and freshness - Mina's Fish House 5, Onodera 5 - and the second is a cuisine they don't own yet (Rigo's Spanish-Italian got a 5 on novelty plus atmosphere). Peruvian ceviche is exactly the bridge: lime-cured fish with chili and herbs, which also scratches the tom-yum sourness they love at Olay's.
recommendations.avoids: A modest, family-run dining room rather than a loud bar-restaurant - no repeat of the volume that dropped Restaurant 604 to 3/5.
recommendations.dish: Ceviche mixto, and arroz con mariscos
recommendations.diet_fit: Peruvian menus are seafood-heavy: ceviche, arroz con mariscos, chupe de camarones (shrimp chowder), jalea, plus papa a la huancaína as a starter. Plenty of substantial pescatarian mains.

recommendations.name: Middle Eats
recommendations.reason: Their library has zero Mediterranean or Levantine cooking, and the traits they consistently reward - bright herbs and spice (Olay's), shareable plates for a group (Giovedi), strong value (Onkee's value 5) - all land here. Mezze dining also solves the pescatarian question better than almost any cuisine, so nobody at the table is ordering around a constraint.
recommendations.avoids: A small, fast-casual counter with no sound system, so it avoids the loud-music failing of Monkeypod Kitchen in Kapolei. I don't know this specific kitchen first-hand, hence the modest confidence.
recommendations.diet_fit: Falafel plates and wraps, hummus and baba ghanoush with fresh bread, tabbouleh and fattoush, plus rice platters with vegetables - the pescatarian can order the largest plate on the board without substitutions.

recommendations.name: Water Drop Vegetarian House
recommendations.reason: A genuinely different meal from anything in their thirteen: Buddhist-style Chinese cooking, all the wok technique and braises of a Cantonese kitchen with no meat in the building. Given they rate food above all else and happily ate at plain rooms (Katsumidori food 5, vibe 2), this is a low-risk way to widen the range - and it takes the dietary negotiation off the table entirely.
recommendations.avoids: Quiet, unhurried dining room - nothing like the noise that gave Restaurant 604 quiet 1 and Monkeypod Kitchen a 3/5.
recommendations.diet_fit: Fully vegetarian: braised tofu and mushroom claypots, mock-meat stir-fries, noodle and rice plates, hot-and-sour soup and greens. Every main on the menu is safe for the pescatarian.

recommendations.name: O’Kims
recommendations.reason: Onkee Korean Grill House is a 5/5 with food 5, service 5, value 5 - Korean flavours clearly land hard with this household. But rather than another grill house, this is modern Korean small plates in Kakaako with outdoor seating and a proper drinks list, which also picks up the terrace-and-mocktails thread from The Kini Room and Mina's Fish House.
recommendations.avoids: Avoids the two things they penalised: dated interiors (Roy's, Katsumidori) and blasting music (Monkeypod). Also avoids being a meat-grill format, which would leave the pescatarian with banchan only.
recommendations.diet_fit: Not a tabletop-meat place: haemul pajeon (seafood scallion pancake), soondubu jjigae in seafood or vegetable form, japchae, kimchi fried rice without meat, and tofu dishes give the pescatarian real mains. Confirm the jjigae broth is not beef-based.

recommendations.name: TsuruTonTan
recommendations.reason: They have two sushi houses rated 4-5 but no Japanese noodle cooking at all. TsuruTonTan is handmade sanuki udon in giant bowls, served in a polished modern room in Waikiki - so it extends the Japanese-craft thread from Kaiten Sushi Ginza Onodera while fixing the tired-interior grumble they had about Katsumidori Sushi Tokyo.
recommendations.avoids: A calm, well-designed dining room, not the loud-music environment that sank Monkeypod Kitchen for them.
recommendations.dish: Mentaiko cream udon, or the tempura udon with a proper shrimp tempura
recommendations.diet_fit: Kake and zaru udon in kombu-bonito dashi, mentaiko cream udon, tempura udon with shrimp and vegetables, plus seafood tempura sides - several substantial pescatarian bowls.

recommendations.name: Arancino di Mare
recommendations.reason: Their Italian scores (cino 4, Giovedi 4, Rigo 5) say they want the real thing plus a good room; Rigo won on atmosphere, cino lost on darkness. Arancino di Mare is the seafood-led branch of that cooking - Italian pasta technique applied to island fish and uni - which is the exact intersection of their Italian 4s and their Mina's Fish House 5.
recommendations.avoids: Bright, airy hotel dining room, so no repeat of cino's dark interior or Roy's dated one, and the volume stays conversational unlike Restaurant 604.
recommendations.dish: Sea urchin spaghetti in a cream sauce, served in the shell
recommendations.diet_fit: Seafood-forward Italian: uni spaghetti, vongole, seafood risotto, spaghetti pomodoro and caprese - the pescatarian has more choice than anyone else at the table.

recommendations.name: Pizza Mamo
recommendations.reason: Moku Kitchen got a 4 on the strength of its pizza. Pizza Mamo is a serious upgrade on that one axis - a tiny Chinatown shop doing naturally leavened pies with local toppings - so instead of another full-service restaurant with pizza on the menu, they get the best version of the thing they already liked.
recommendations.avoids: No live music and no sound system, which is what dragged Monkeypod Kitchen down to 3/5; this is a walk-up counter with a handful of seats.
recommendations.dish: A slice or whole pie with the local-tomato and cheese base; the sourdough crust is the point
recommendations.diet_fit: Margherita and other cheese/vegetable pies, plus salads - straightforward pescatarian eating. Skip the meat-topped pies.

recommendations.name: Búho Cocina y Cantina
recommendations.reason: The Kini Room earned vibe 5 and value 5 for terrace seating, happy hour and mocktails; Mina's Fish House earned a 5 partly for the view. Búho is a Waikiki rooftop with open-air tables, a real drinks bar that makes credible non-alcoholic versions, and ceviche and fish tacos - a cuisine they have never rated, which is the point.
recommendations.avoids: This is the one pick where I'd watch the noise they flagged at Monkeypod Kitchen - ask for a table on the open-air edge rather than near the bar, where the room stays at Kini Room volume rather than Restaurant 604 volume.
recommendations.dish: Fish tacos and the ceviche, with a mocktail from the agua fresca side of the list
recommendations.diet_fit: Ceviche, grilled fish tacos, shrimp tacos, guacamole and queso fundido, and vegetable/bean tacos - multiple full pescatarian plates.

recommendations.name: Thai Vientiane Restaurant
recommendations.reason: Olay's Thai Lao Cuisine is one of their 5/5 regulars - and the tell is the 'Lao' half, which is where the herb-heavy, sour-hot cooking they keep ordering (tom yum, curries) actually comes from. Thai Vientiane is the other Lao-leaning kitchen on this island, so it deepens that specific interest rather than adding a generic fifth Thai place.
recommendations.avoids: A small family dining room with no live music, avoiding the volume issue that capped Monkeypod Kitchen and Restaurant 604. Also free of Olay's own drawback for them - paid parking - being in a residential stretch.
recommendations.diet_fit: Tom yum with shrimp, green/red/panang curry with tofu or fish, pad thai with shrimp or tofu, green papaya salad and larb made with tofu on request - several substantial pescatarian mains. Ask them to leave the pork out of the papaya salad dressing.

recommendations.name: Tadka Indian Cuisine
recommendations.reason: Nothing in their thirteen is South Asian, yet the flavour profile they rate highest - the chili-and-spice depth of Olay's curries at 5/5, the shared-plate format they liked at Giovedi - transfers directly. Indian is also the cuisine where the pescatarian orders best, so the whole table eats at full strength instead of working around a constraint.
recommendations.avoids: A modest sit-down dining room rather than a bar with a sound system, so it steers clear of the loud-music complaint that held Monkeypod Kitchen to 3/5. I don't know this particular kitchen, so confidence is deliberately low.
recommendations.diet_fit: Paneer dishes (saag paneer, paneer tikka masala), dal makhani, chana masala, vegetable biryani and fish or shrimp curry if offered - all full mains for a pescatarian, with naan and rice.
